newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says Northwest stake sale an option.
newsitem.headline: KLM says Northwest stake sale an option.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said Wednesday that the sale of its shares in Northwest Airlines was one of the options open to it in resolving the partners' long-running dispute over KLM's Northwest holding.
"One of the options is a possible sale of shares to Northwest," said KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuener.
Wellhuener declined to comment, however, on the likelihood of a Northwest sale going ahead, saying only: "It is an option ... How important (an option) it is, we will not comment."
He said talks at management level to resolve the dispute over KLM's 19 percent Northwest stake were continuing, and KLM would not comment on their progress.
Northwest, which is based in Eagan, Minn., has accused KLM of trying to extend its influence over it.

Dutch De Telegraaf newspaper said in a front-page article Wednesday that KLM was mulling the sale of its Northwest stake to further the lucrative operational alliance between the two, which until now has been based on short-term contracts.
Analysts hailed the news as a positive development, saying a share sell-off was not at all unlikely and represented "an ideal way" to further the KLM-Northwest alliance.
Until now the lucrative alliance between the two airlines, under which they operate as a single carrier on transatlantic routes, has been based on short-term contracts.
The two carriers have been locked in a long-running dispute over KLM's rights to a further 5 percent Northwest stake under an option exercisable in 1998.
KLM is currently suing Northwest over a shareholder rights plan capping its holding at current levels. Northwest in turn has accused KLM of being out to gain control.
Outgoing KLM President Pieter Bouw said in May that the Dutch carrier was in talks to resolve the boardroom battle, adding that he hoped to announce a positive outcome within the foreseeable future.
But he declined then to comment on speculation KLM was prepared to sell its Northwest stake in return for a multi-year partnership agreement.
